title.en: Guarantee of profit to a partner

say.en: A skilled chef joins a restaurant firm only if she is promised at least 30,000 rupees a year. If her share comes to less, who pays the difference? This is a guarantee of profit. In this lesson: Find the deficiency when profit is guaranteed.
Share the deficiency among the guaranteeing partners.

title.en: Meaning of guarantee and treatment of deficiency

body.en: A *guarantee* fixes the minimum profit a partner (usually a new one) will get. First share profit in the normal ratio. If the guaranteed partner's share is below the guarantee, the deficiency is borne by the partner(s) who gave the guarantee, in the agreed ratio — or in their own profit sharing ratio if no ratio is given. If the actual share is more, the partner simply gets the actual share.
body.kn: ಖಾತರಿ ಎಂದರೆ ಪಾಲುದಾರನಿಗೆ ಸಿಗುವ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಲಾಭ. ಮೊದಲು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಂಚಿ. ಪಾಲು ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೆ ಕೊರತೆಯನ್ನು ಖಾತರಿ ನೀಡಿದ ಪಾಲುದಾರರು ಒಪ್ಪಿದ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಭರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ.

say.en: A guarantee fixes the minimum profit a partner usually a new one will get. First share profit in the normal ratio. If the guaranteed partner's share is below the guarantee, the deficiency is borne by the partners who gave the guarantee, in the agreed ratio, or in their own profit sharing ratio if no ratio is given. If the actual share is more, the partner simply gets the actual share. Deficiency equals guaranteed amount - actual share.
say.kn: ಖಾತರಿ ಎಂದರೆ ಪಾಲುದಾರನಿಗೆ ಸಿಗುವ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಲಾಭ. ಮೊದಲು ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಂಚಿ. ಪಾಲು ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾದರೆ ಕೊರತೆಯನ್ನು ಖಾತರಿ ನೀಡಿದ ಪಾಲುದಾರರು ಒಪ್ಪಿದ ಅನುಪಾತದಲ್ಲಿ ಭರಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ.

say.en: Borne by guaranteeing partners in agreed ratio.
If actual share is greater than or equal to guarantee, no adjustment.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. A, B and C share profits 3:2:1. C is guaranteed a minimum of ₹30,000; any deficiency is borne by A and B in 3:2. Profit is ₹1,20,000. Distribute it.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. A, B and C share profits 3:2:1. C is guaranteed a minimum of 30,000 rupees; any deficiency is borne by A and B in 3:2. Profit is 1,20,000 rupees. Distribute it.
Normal shares: A 60,000, B 40,000, C 20,000.
Deficiency for C equals 30,000 minus 20,000 equals 10,000 rupees.
A bears 10,000 times 3 over 5 equals 6,000 rupees; B bears 4,000 rupees.
So the answer is A 54,000 rupees; B 36,000 rupees; C 30,000 rupees.
